In the age of modern artistic works and other theme based competition, the traditional Bengali way of practicing the greatest festival of Bengalese is slowly losing its existence. Hence in order to maintain the legacy of this greatest festival and to keep the age old heritage into existence, we at 37 Pally Sarbojanin Durgotsab O Saradiya Sammelan do not believe in any theme based puja. We practice the very same Sanatani style of pujo for the last 73 years. This year too we are into our traditional way of celebrating the festival without any change in our customary way of celebration. Hope we can maintain this legacy and not let lose ourselves from the ties of heritage.

The pandal is designed as an imaginative chandi mondap of the ancient Bengal tribes during the medieval age. The pandal is beautifully decorated by madhubani paintings and other artistic works, completely to be painted by actual madhubani artists from Bihar and Jharkhand.

The theme this year is basically the village environment of Bankura,a well known district in Bengal famous for its teracotta temples and thakur dalans. We are trying to depict one such scenario of the thakur dalans of Bankura where uma or goddess Durga is worshipped just as a daughter. Besides the pictorial demography, we are also keeping in mind about the need for a more environment friendly ways of celebrating this festival and hence the materials that we are using this year is completely eco-friendly and non hazardous to the environment.

South Asian countries are well known for their fabulous truck art. the designs are mainly rajasthani folk art based. this time we are also trying to depict such art in our puja pandel. The artist are very talented and hence we are trying to uplift this work and make this work established as a form of art in the society.
The omnipresence of god is the basis of the concept. Fodder,an important element of village life is the epicenter of our theme this year. this is the debut year for us in the field of theme puja.

This year our theme is inspired by YANTRA "a tool for contemplation, concentration and meditation. Any YANTRA consists of simple triangle shapes. The triangle (TRIKONA) is the symbol of SHAKTI, the feminine energy or aspect of Creation. The triangle pointing down represents the YONI, the symbol of the supreme source of the Universe, and when the triangle is pointing upwards it signifies intense spiritual aspiration. The fire is always oriented upwards, thus the correlation with the upward triangle "SHIVA KONA. On the other hand, the downward pointing triangle signifies the element of water which always tends to flown and occupy the lowest possible position. This triangle is known as SHAKTI KONA. The intersection of two geometric forms represents forces that are even more intense, the union of PURUSHA and PRAKRITI or SHIVA and SHAKTI, without which there could be no Creation.

Our urban civilization is attuned to brick, wood and stone. the moment the processes of urbanization has gathered a momentum, the bandwagon of civilization seems to have taken a great sited in the swathe of the world. However, at this occasion "Haridevpur New Sporting Club" make an endeavor to unravel such a phenomenon which remains dormant underneath the veneer of glitz and glitter of ever expanding urbanization for centuries together. Most likely it would continue to remain obscured in the abyss as long as a human civilization survives. It is a long story as to how a woman turns into a phenomenal "REJA" and her attachment to a brick kiln. so we just focus on their plights, pangs of living side a brick kiln she in her early teens enrolls herself as a laborer, at a time when an upcoming girl ought to unfurl herself in the portals of learning and playing, sadly, they are a far cry from her. Her life remains confined to slushy brick kiln to let magnificent buildings spring up. They cater to the materials at the cost of their industry, sacrificing their own dreams, hopes and aspirations. In return they are subjected to privation, humiliation and sexual abuse. They are their lifelong companions. Our puja sanctuary will be embellished with all these scenarios, sculpted by our accomplished artiste Sri Animesh Das. given this theme related to the female workers of brick kiln, by laying brick one after another along with grating hammering on chisel, the tales of their struggling life will find pregnant revelation in the theme of "EI GOLPER NAA,M KONO NEI" (THEREN IS NO NAME IN THIS STORY).

We are going through one of the most harrowing times of the 21st century. The very existence of mankind is being questioned during this pandemic COVID19. Our normal lifestyle has been interrupted; we are helplessly confined to our houses. Some, however, have come forward without fear of their own lives. They are our true warriors! They have not returned to their families for days on end. Forgetting rest, entertainment, sleep, they have dedicated themselves to the service of mankind. Donning their PPE kits, disregarding their own discomfort, they have become our true protectors. Our prayers to Mother Goddess Durga are for these COVID warriors. Let Her protect them from all harm and let Her stand as their protector In this festival, we are going to narrate the stories of these warriors -- they, who have returned our near and dear ones safely to our homes. We remember them amidst these festivities and pay our deepest regards to them.

In our 74th year of HALSIBAGAN SARBAJANIN DURGOTSAV 2018, our presentation for this year is to introduce folk art & ancient culture to the people. Over time, folk art has gone a long way. Cultural identities, values & aesthetics are expressed through folk art. Folklore has been created from rural life. People are creative since ancient times. The type of creativity has been changed over time. A variety of arts have been evolved around the world since ancient time. Some of the arts are extinct and some are still unrevealed. In the present time, the beauty of antiquity has been lost due to mechanization and modernizations. Some of the folk art has been preserved in the archives and some in exhibitions where the so-called general people are unable to reach. The DURGOTSAV OF BENGAL is such a festival where all kind of people irrespective of any caste and creed gather en masse and meet with each other to share their feelings. We have just tried to represent the idea depicting the energy, soul, and divinity of a mother in the form of the deity of MA MAHAMAYA and folk arts as well to everyone through this festival.

The Mahabharata is an ancient Indian epic where the main story revolves around two branches of a family - the Pandavas and Kauravas - who, in the Kurukshetra War, battle for the throne of Hastinapura. Interwoven into this narrative are several smaller stories about people dead or living, and philosophical discourses. Krishna-Dwaipayan Vyasa, himself a character in the epic, composed it; as, according to tradition, he dictated the verses and Ganesha wrote them down. At 100,000 verses, it is the longest epic poem ever written, generally thought to have been composed in the 4th century BCE or earlier. The events in the epic play out in the Indian subcontinent and surrounding areas. It was first narrated by a student of Vyasa at a snake-sacrifice of the great-grandson of one of the major characters of the story.

Our theme this year is "Kathputli o Rajeshwari" and conceptualized by Sri Debabrata Singha, a budding but renowned artist of the modern era. We are portraying the picture of a concept that soothes the beholder both visually and spiritually. The "Kathputli o Rajeshwari" concept is a manifestation of our penchant to blissfully channelize our future generation not only to appreciate the beauty of the waning art forms of India but also to grow an attachment towards the rich heritage of the country with an underlying intention of conservation of the 'Kathputli' art form. Quite likely, a pleasant grandiose will be portrayed in all our endeavors, starting from the ambience, to the interiors and the decor. In our theme, we are aiming to portray the image of the Mother Goddess with her usual grandiose and ethnicity amidst the Khuri Village hutment resort of Jaisalmer. Through our theme, we aim to make this puja, one to look up to not only in this year but also the coming years.

"Go Green-grow trees" concept is a manifestation of our penchant to encourage tree plantation. Quite likely, greenery will be portrayed in all our endeavors, starting from the ambience, to the interiors and the dÃ©cor. In our theme, we are aiming to portray the image of the Mother Goddess as an eternal mother figure that we witness in the villages of Bengal. Lacking the usual grandeur of Rajrajeshwari, our versatile village mother, clad in ethnic attire would be seen surrounded by her four little children with their respective pets, happy and content in their frugal abode which is nothing more than a thatched hut. The hut is surrounded by trees and there is greenery all around. Even the feisty Mahishasur shall be seen immersed in deep penance and there is peace prevailing everywhere.

This year 2019, we are going to organize 20th Durga Puja, where we would like to emphasize rural Bengal craft-decorating a fictional temple with bamboo string, cane bucket to reflect its abundance. Our State West Bengal is famous for its cane and Bamboo craft but now a days those are very rarely visible in common mass lifestyle. Bamboo grass, some flexible woody stalk which are widely cultivated here in rural area is used for making common household accessories. Cane sticks are skillfully tied and bent together to make various furniture, racks, swing, baskets. Sometimes those cane string are used for artificial decoration too. We are displaying those all while decorate our idol pandel and hoping to bring them in light on account of Durga Puja.

"Elem Putul Deshe", the Folk Puppetry of Bengal. Pandal will also be decorated with various aspects of wooden Puppets and wooden handicraft. The idol of Debi Durga will be decorated from a single piece of wooden, keeping the essence of Theme.

We want to bring into life the different dimensions of 'Chou Dance', a widely popular folk dance form of the district of mainly Purulia in our state. The Pandal will be decorated with Chhou masks and other accessories. The idol of Debi Durga will have an essence of the theme.
